newsitem.title: USA: Florida governor asks for federal aid for riot city.
newsitem.headline: Florida governor asks for federal aid for riot city.

text.p: Florida's governor appealed Thursday to federal officials for emergency disaster assistance after racial unrest in St. Petersburg during the past month.

Governor Lawton Chiles requested assistance from the Small Business Administration after nearly 70 incidents of arson and other damage to property that state officials say have cost business owners, citizens and local government millions of dollars.

The governor's request comes nearly a month after rioting residents burned businesses, homes and vehicles after a white police officer shot and killed an 18-year-old black male following a traffic stop in South St. Petersburg.
Rioting broke out again Nov. 14, when a grand jury cleared the officer of wrongdoing.
"The civil unrest and disturbance resulted in numerous fires and caused a severe loss to a section of the community's businesses and housing," Chiles wrote SBA district Michael Allen.

State labor department officials have requested $1.1 million in emergency assistance under the federal Job Training and Partnership Act to provide assistance to workers displaced by fires that burned at least 29 businesses.
In addition to direct aid, Chiles is seeking low-interest loans for area business and home owners, many of whom were uninsured.
